en.title: Sleep & Stress
en.who: Guests who mark trouble falling asleep, waking at 3 am, waking up unrefreshed, stressed all day and wired at night, jet lag, or stress that goes to the stomach.
studyWhy: the liver, and why sleep routes through it

say: I know that feeling. You're exhausted, you lie down, and your head just won't switch off. Or you finally fall asleep and you're up again at 3 am.
feel.tip: Say back what they marked, in their words. Then ask: "Is it falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up tired?"

say: Honestly, I've been there. [Your story in a line or two: when it was, what it felt like, what you tried that didn't work.]
felt.tip: Your own story, or someone close to you ("my mom", "a friend from work"). No story yet? "A lot of the people I talk to say exactly the same thing." Never make one up.

say: What I learned is that the body has a stress alarm that's supposed to switch off at night. When stress stays high all day, it's still on at bedtime, so you're tired but your brain is on watch.
The calming signals are built from nutrients like magnesium and the B vitamins, and stress burns through them faster. So it's not only in your head: your body is short on what it needs to calm down.
So this is what I'd start with.
found.tip: Two or three sentences, then go to the map. Pick the row that matches what they marked.

map: Cal Mag D (or Magnesium), with dinner
Raw material for the calming signals
Stressed all day, wired at night
Calms the stress system; judge it at about eight weeks
Stress uses up the B vitamins faster
Wakes at 3 am, late dinners or drinks
Liver Support, in the evening with Vitamin B
Eases the work the body does through the night
The gut and the brain talk both ways; give it five to eight weeks
Sleep Gummies (3 mg melatonin), the odd night only
A clock signal, not a sleeping pill. Not for children, pregnancy or anyone on blood thinners
Wants it all in one box
The core set in one pack
en.ask: Based on what you told me, I'd start with the magnesium, the ashwagandha and the B vitamins. Do you want to take it home tonight?
en.doctor: Loud snoring, pauses in breathing, or trouble sleeping most nights for three months? See a doctor first. Never change sleeping pills or antidepressants without the doctor. Pregnant or breastfeeding: no ashwagandha.

zh.title: 睡眠与压力
zh.who: 适合在问卷里勾了入睡难、半夜三点醒、睡够了还是没精神、白天发蔫晚上精神、倒时差，或者一紧张胃就不舒服的客人。
studyWhy: 肝，以及为什么睡眠问题要从肝入手

say: 我懂那种感觉。明明累得不行，躺下了脑子却停不下来。或者好不容易睡着了，半夜三点又醒。
feel.tip: 用对方自己的话，把问卷上勾的说回去。然后问一句：“是睡不着、睡不稳，还是醒来还很累？”

say: 说实话，我也经历过。[你的故事，一两句就好：什么时候、什么感觉、试过什么没用。]
felt.tip: 讲你自己的，或者身边人的（“我妈妈”“我一个同事”）。还没有故事？就说：“我身边很多朋友也是这样。”千万别编。

say: 我后来学到，身体里有一个压力警报，到了晚上本该关掉。可是压力一整天都很大，睡前它还开着，所以人很累，大脑却还在值班。
让人平静下来的信号，是用镁、B族这些营养素做出来的，压力越大用得越快。所以不只是想太多，身体里让你静下来的原料也不够了。
所以，我会先从这个开始。
found.tip: 两三句就够，然后看下面的对照表，挑跟对方勾的那一项对得上的。

map: 白天压力大，晚上反而精神
让压力系统平静下来，大约八周看效果
半夜三点醒、晚饭晚或常喝酒
护肝片，晚上和B族一起吃
肠道和大脑是双向沟通的，给它五到八周
甜梦睡眠软糖（含3毫克褪黑素），偶尔用
是时钟信号，不是安眠药。儿童、孕期、服用抗凝药的人不用
zh.ask: 按你刚才说的，我建议先从镁、南非醉茄和B族这三样开始。今天要不要先带回去？
zh.doctor: 打鼾很响、睡眠中有呼吸暂停，或者连续三个月大多数晚上都睡不好？请先去看医生。安眠药、抗抑郁药一定要在医生指导下调整。怀孕或哺乳期不吃南非醉茄。
